On 21 June 2026 , the football world turned its eyes to a compelling World Cup encounter between Türkiye and Paraguay . The match featured contrasting styles and tactical intrigue that kept the crowd on the edge of their seats throughout the contest. Explosive Start and Early Advantage The match ignited instantly, and Paraguay wasted no time in establishing their presence. Just two minutes into the game, Matías Galarza silenced the Turkish fans with a clinical left-footed strike from outside the box, finding the bottom right corner after being set up by Julio Enciso . This early blow forced Türkiye into an immediate offensive response, as they looked to break down a resilient South American defensive line. As the first half progressed, Türkiye ramped up the pressure. Arda Güler and Kenan Yildiz were central to their creative efforts, with Yildiz forcing a spectacular save from Orlando Gill around the half-hour mark. Despite the mounting pressure and several corner opportunities, the Paraguayan defense held firm, although the physical nature of the game saw Galarza pick up an early yellow card. Discipline and Drama Before the Break The narrative took a dramatic turn in the closing moments of the first half. Deep into stoppage time, following a VAR review, Miguel Almirón was shown a straight red card, leaving Paraguay to navigate the remainder of the match with ten men. The dismissal energized the Turkish side, who unleashed a flurry of attempts through Hakan Çalhanoglu and Ismail Yüksek , but they could not find the equalizer before the whistle blew. The Turkish Onslaught Against Ten Men With a numerical advantage, Türkiye dominated possession in the second half, introducing Baris Alper Yilmaz and Can Uzun to intensify their attack. The pressure was relentless; Merih Demiral became a frequent threat in the box, testing Orlando Gill with multiple headers and long-range efforts. Gill remained the protagonist of the afternoon, producing a series of vital saves to keep his side ahead. Paraguay 's resilience was tested further as injuries forced several substitutions, including the departures of Diego Gómez , Matías Galarza , and Julio Enciso . Despite these setbacks, the defensive unit led by Gustavo Gómez and Júnior Alonso threw themselves in front of every shot, blocking efforts from Güler and Çalhanoglu as the clock ticked down. Final Desperation and Defensive Heroics The closing stages were characterized by desperate Turkish attacks and heroic Paraguayan defending. Can Uzun and Deniz Gül both saw chances flash wide of the post as the game entered seven minutes of added time. In the very last second of play, Hakan Çalhanoglu had a golden opportunity from a set-piece, but his right-footed shot whistled just past the left post. The final whistle confirmed a heroic 1-0 victory for Paraguay , leaving Türkiye to reflect on a night of missed opportunities.

matches.description: Watch Australia vs Turkey highlights and goals from World Cup 2026 on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on June 13, 2026. Fans gathered in anticipation for a crucial World Cup clash between two nations with contrasting footballing philosophies. The atmosphere was electric as the teams prepared to battle for vital points on the international stage. Clinical Socceroos Strike First On June 13, 2026, in front of a capacity crowd of 52,497, the story of the match was one of efficiency versus possession. Turkiye dominated the ball from the outset, eventually commanding 70% of possession, but they lacked the finishing touch required to break through. After an early scare where Ugurcan Cakir nearly gifted an opening, Australia took the lead in the 27th minute. Paul Okon-Engstler provided a perfectly weighted assist for Nestory Irankunda , who clinicaly dispatched a right-footed shot to give the Socceroos the advantage. Turkiye attempted to respond immediately through the creative sparks of Arda Guler and Hakan Calhanoglu . Despite numerous corners and long-range efforts, the Turkish attackers found themselves frustrated by a disciplined Australian defensive block. As the halftime whistle blew, the scoreboard reflected Australia's ability to capitalize on their limited opportunities. Metcalfe Seals the Points The second half saw Turkiye ramp up the pressure, introducing Kenan Yildiz and Yunus Akgun to find a way back into the game. However, the Australian defense, anchored by the towering Harry Souttar , remained resolute. Souttar was instrumental in the closing stages, making several key interceptions and blocking a goal-bound effort from Kenan Yildiz in stoppage time. The decisive blow arrived in the 75th minute. Connor Metcalfe picked up the ball outside the penalty area and unleashed a stunning left-footed strike that flew past Cakir into the net. This second goal effectively ended the Turkish resistance. Despite a late offside call against Merih Demiral and a flurry of desperate attacks, Australia held firm to secure a famous victory, with Paul Okon-Engstler earning plaudits for a Man of the Match caliber performance.
